analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Bonds Lose Momentum As Stocks Rebound
key_insights: RBNZ left rates unchanged at 2.75%, a surprise to markets, citing global uncertainty weighing on domestic demand. It warned further tightening is likely needed but conditional on the outlook.

Australian trimmed mean CPI rose to 1.0% q/q from 0.8%, and y/y rose to 3.7% from 3.6%. RBA Governor Bullock told the Senate committee that upside inflation risks have materialised or are materialising and inflation will likely exceed the August base case.

Markets price an 86% chance of a 25bp RBA hike next week, up from 60% on Tuesday. 3y futures hit a low of 95.05 on the inflation release and recovered to 95.08. The IR strip closed down as much as seven ticks, led by the whites in a flattening move, and IRM7/M8 fell four ticks to -22.

US fixed income was weaker in Asia, with TY down to a low of 105-26 and the SOFR strip down as much as 3.5 ticks. Drivers were the Australian inflation data, a WSJ report that the US told several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterms, and a better equity tone.

Equities rebounded, with the Kospi up 6.63% on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected SK Hynix profits and a plan to return more money to shareholders. SK Hynix warned that component shortages vital to Nvidia will persist until 2030, keeping prices and operating margins elevated. Recent tech weakness had supported fixed income, and buyers have now returned to equities.

Activity after the Fed meeting was in line with recent volume averages and skewed to the downside in fixed income. Flows included a 2s20s block steepener, a TYZ6 105/103.50 put spread bought for 16 in 3k, and Week 5 October TY 105.25 puts bought for 9 in 5k, which expire tomorrow.

UBS sees no notable upside interest in USTs now that equities have found support. SOFR accounts are using low-premium plays to cover the possibility that the Fed does not hike in December. One notable flow was a buyer of 3.5k SFRF7 95.5625/95.6875/96.125 call ladder for a 0.25 credit, and there has been little recent interest in fading call skew.

CTAs remain heavily short duration, with short covering picking up in Japan and Australia. A move toward 4.8% to 4.85% in USTs could trigger more meaningful short covering. In credit, long liquidations have turned into outright shorts across most markets, with US IG the exception at a marginally positive signal.

UBS economics expected no Fed change, with two dissenters (Logan and Hammack), though it could be one or three. They expected Chair Warsh to say there is more work to do on elevated inflation, to lean on the 'trend not the data point' framing, and to keep the press conference brief.
The US 5y auction tailed by 0.3bp, the 12th straight 5y tail. Bid-to-cover was 2.33 vs a last-six average of 2.31. Indirects took 60% (from 54.3%), directs 29.4% and dealers 10.6%.

The European Commission is reportedly considering revenue from a global tax agreement to fund the next seven-year EU budget. The CORE corporate tax on revenues over EUR 100 mn is the most unpopular option, especially in Germany, and Macron suggested using part of the tax on multinationals instead.
